neighbours.label: the pieces 'udge' / 'ud' in sludge, sludgy and fudge when the word splits
fire: The factory dumped its toxic sludge into the nearest river.
After the flood, a layer of sludge covered every street in town.
Workers pumped the oily sludge out of the ship's tanks.
Decades of runoff left a sludgy mess at the bottom of the lake.
Treatment plants dry the sewage sludge before they burn it.
Grandpa cut each square of walnut fudge with a warm knife.
Waste sludge from the tannery smelled terrible in the summer.
Thick sludgy coffee sat at the bottom of the old pot.
quiet: The factory dumped its toxic waste into the nearest river.
After the flood, a layer of mud covered every street in town.
Workers pumped the heavy fuel out of the ship's tanks.
Decades of runoff left a green film at the bottom of the lake.
Treatment plants dry the filtered solids before they burn them.
Grandpa cut each square of walnut cake with a warm knife.
Rotting hides from the tannery smelled terrible in the summer.
Thick black coffee sat at the bottom of the old pot.
